reading.body:
Every freely available video resource listed here covers the conceptual and software layers of AI, not the physical infrastructure that makes large-scale AI possible.

The seven entries span mathematical foundations, graduate coursework, practitioner conference talks, and major product announcements. One exception is the NVIDIA GTC keynote, where the AI hardware roadmap is announced each year, making it the single entry that connects directly to compute supply. The rest address how models work or how to build with them, not what powers them or where that power comes from.

That gap matters for readers of this site. A learner who completes every resource here will understand gradient descent, transformer architecture, and how to build on large language models, but will have little grounding in data center construction, grid capacity, or the physical constraints on AI scaling. The data covers what it covers, and does not pretend otherwise.
